supplementaryControls.title: Organizational context understood and reviewed
supplementaryControls.description: Identify and periodically review the internal and external issues that bear on the ISMS

supplementaryControls.title: Interested parties and their requirements identified
supplementaryControls.description: Maintain a list of stakeholders and the security requirements the ISMS takes on from them

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS scope defined and maintained
supplementaryControls.description: Define, document and keep current the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS established and maintained
supplementaryControls.description: Operate the ISMS as a maintained management system with defined processes and interactions

supplementaryControls.title: Top management leadership and commitment
supplementaryControls.description: Have top management sponsor, resource and promote the ISMS

supplementaryControls.title: Top-level information security policy
supplementaryControls.description: Issue and communicate an overarching information security policy approved by top management

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS roles and authorities assigned
supplementaryControls.description: Assign and communicate ISMS responsibilities and authorities, including reporting on ISMS performance

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS risks and opportunities planned
supplementaryControls.description: Identify risks and opportunities to the ISMS and plan actions to address them

supplementaryControls.title: Information security risk assessment process
supplementaryControls.description: Define risk criteria and run a repeatable process to identify, analyse and evaluate information security risks

supplementaryControls.title: Information security risk treatment process
supplementaryControls.description: Treat assessed risks, determine the necessary controls, maintain the Statement of Applicability and obtain risk owner approval

supplementaryControls.title: Information security objectives set and planned
supplementaryControls.description: Set measurable information security objectives and plan how they will be achieved and evaluated

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS changes planned
supplementaryControls.description: Plan and control changes to the ISMS

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS resources provided
supplementaryControls.description: Determine and provide the resources the ISMS needs

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS competence ensured
supplementaryControls.description: Define required competence for security-relevant roles, close gaps and keep records

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS awareness ensured
supplementaryControls.description: Make personnel aware of the security policy, their contribution to the ISMS and the effect of not conforming

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS communication planned
supplementaryControls.description: Determine and follow internal and external communication needs for the ISMS

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS documented information controlled
supplementaryControls.description: Create, update and control ISMS documents and records

supplementaryControls.title: Operational planning and control
supplementaryControls.description: Plan, run and control the processes that deliver ISMS requirements, including outsourced ones

supplementaryControls.title: Information security risk assessments performed
supplementaryControls.description: Perform and record risk assessments at planned intervals and on significant change

supplementaryControls.title: Information security risk treatment implemented
supplementaryControls.description: Implement the risk treatment plan and record the outcome

supplementaryControls.title: ISMS performance monitored and measured
supplementaryControls.description: Define, run and evaluate monitoring and measurement of security performance and ISMS effectiveness

supplementaryControls.title: Internal audit programme
supplementaryControls.description: Plan and run an internal ISMS audit programme with impartial auditors and reported results

supplementaryControls.title: Management review
supplementaryControls.description: Hold planned management reviews of the ISMS and record the resulting decisions

supplementaryControls.title: Continual improvement of the ISMS
supplementaryControls.description: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the ISMS

supplementaryControls.title: Nonconformity and corrective action process
supplementaryControls.description: Handle nonconformities, find and remove their causes, verify the fix and keep records

requirements.title: Organizational context
requirements.text: Work out which internal and external factors shape the organization's ability to reach the results its security management system is meant to deliver, and keep that picture current.

requirements.title: Stakeholder needs
requirements.text: Identify the parties with a stake in information security, such as customers, regulators and staff, and decide which of their needs and expectations the ISMS has to address.

mappings.rationale: Legal, statutory and regulatory requirements (A.5.31) are one important subset of stakeholder requirements; contractual and other stakeholder expectations are not covered by it, so the mapping is partial.

requirements.title: ISMS scope
requirements.text: Set and document the boundaries of the management system, taking into account the organizational context, stakeholder requirements and the interfaces with anything left outside the scope.

requirements.title: ISMS processes
requirements.text: Establish, run, maintain and keep improving a management system, including the processes it needs and how they interact.

requirements.title: Leadership commitment
requirements.text: Top management visibly backs the ISMS: it makes sure security objectives fit the business direction, that resources are available, and that security is part of ordinary business processes.

mappings.rationale: Management responsibilities (A.5.4) covers managers enforcing security policy, a narrower duty than top management's overall ownership and sponsorship of the ISMS.

requirements.title: Security policy
requirements.text: Top management sets an information security policy that fits the organization, gives a basis for objectives, commits to meeting requirements and to improvement, and is documented and communicated.

mappings.rationale: Policies for information security (A.5.1) covers approving and reviewing the policy set; the top-level policy also carries specific commitments and communication expectations that A.5.1 does not spell out.

requirements.title: Roles and authorities
requirements.text: Assign and communicate who is responsible, and has the authority, for ensuring the ISMS conforms and for reporting on its performance to top management.

mappings.rationale: Information security roles and responsibilities (A.5.2) covers assigning security roles generally; the clause specifically requires responsibility for ISMS conformity and for reporting to top management.

requirements.title: Planning for risks and opportunities
requirements.text: When planning the ISMS, use the organizational context and stakeholder needs to identify the risks and opportunities that must be addressed, and plan how to act on them and check the results.

requirements.title: Risk assessment process
requirements.text: Define and apply a repeatable process for identifying, analysing and evaluating information security risks against agreed criteria, and keep records of the results.

requirements.title: Risk treatment process
requirements.text: Select treatments for the assessed risks, decide which controls are required and compare them against Annex A, document which apply and why in a Statement of Applicability, and have risk owners approve the plan and the remaining risk.

requirements.title: Security objectives
requirements.text: Set measurable security objectives at relevant functions and levels that align with the policy, and plan what will be done, by whom, with what resources, by when, and how results will be evaluated.

requirements.title: Planning of changes
requirements.text: When the management system needs to change, carry the change out in a planned way rather than ad hoc.

requirements.title: Resources
requirements.text: Determine and provide the people, infrastructure, budget and other resources needed to establish, run and improve the ISMS.

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.text: Decide what skills the people who affect security performance need, make sure they have them through education, training or experience, and keep evidence of it.

mappings.rationale: Awareness, education and training (A.6.3) is one way to build competence, but the clause also covers defining the skills needed, competence gained through experience and keeping evidence, so the mapping is partial.

requirements.title: Awareness
requirements.text: Make sure people working under the organization's control know the security policy, how they contribute to the ISMS, and what follows if they do not conform.

mappings.rationale: The awareness and training programme in A.6.3 delivers this awareness; the clause frames what people should understand in relation to the ISMS itself, so the mapping is partial.

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.text: Decide what will be communicated about information security, when, to whom, by whom and through which channels, both inside and outside the organization.

requirements.title: Documented information
requirements.text: Keep the documentation the ISMS requires and the organization judges necessary, and control how it is created, updated, approved, distributed, stored and retained. Covers 7.5.1 to 7.5.3 as one Requirement.

mappings.rationale: Documented operating procedures (A.5.37) covers documenting operating procedures; the clause applies to all ISMS documented information, including how it is created, updated and controlled, so the mapping is partial.

requirements.title: Operational planning and control
requirements.text: Plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet security requirements and carry out the planned actions, keep evidence that they run as planned, and manage changes and outsourced processes.

requirements.title: Risk assessment in operation
requirements.text: Carry out information security risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes occur, and keep the results on record.

requirements.title: Risk treatment in operation
requirements.text: Put the risk treatment plan into effect and keep a record of the treatment results.

requirements.title: Monitoring and measurement
requirements.text: Decide what to monitor and measure, how and when, and who analyses it, then use the results to judge how well security and the ISMS are performing.

requirements.title: Internal audit
requirements.text: Audit the management system internally at planned intervals against the organization's own requirements and the standard, using a defined programme, impartial auditors and reported, retained results. Covers 9.2.1 and 9.2.2 as one Requirement.

mappings.rationale: Independent review of information security (A.5.35) can be met by internal audit, but the clause sets specific programme, criteria and reporting expectations beyond a periodic independent review, so the mapping is partial.

requirements.title: Management review
requirements.text: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals to confirm it stays suitable, adequate and effective, and records its decisions on improvements and changes. Covers 9.3.1 to 9.3.3 as one Requirement.

requirements.title: Continual improvement
requirements.text: Keep improving the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the management system.

requirements.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
requirements.text: When something does not meet requirements, react to it and deal with the consequences, investigate the cause and fix it so it does not recur, check the fix worked, and keep records.
